title: Customer-Pay Additions to an Insurance Claim Repairs Repair Order
content:
Work the insurer does not pay for may be added to an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order at the customer's expense, in two forms.

## 1. Original-equipment part upgrade

An original-equipment upgrade of an insurer-specified part is allowed only where the repair class allows customer-pay part upgrades, and is charged at the difference between the two part prices on the estimate.

*Hypothetical:* the estimate shows the insurer-specified part at USD 240.00 and the original-equipment part at USD 410.00; the upgrade is charged at USD 170.00.

## 2. Unrelated damage and denied operations

The second form is repair of damage unrelated to the claim (or of operations the insurer denied). The clause under which such work was "charged at the amount on the written customer-pay estimate line" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current pricing basis for these additions.

The unrelated work on one repair order is kept within the class's limit on unrelated-damage labor hours, counted as the labor hours on the signed unrelated-damage consents of the repair order.

*Hypothetical, class limit 8.0 hours:* signed unrelated-damage consents already total 5.5 hours; a further 2.5 hours brings the total to 8.0 hours, within the limit; a further 3.0 hours would bring it to 8.5 hours, beyond it.

## 3. Consent and charge

The sentence "The customer's customer-pay addition consent for that amount is signed." is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis on which the consent is signed and the addition charged. The charge carries the reference of the customer-pay addition consent it rests on.

## 4. Withdrawal of an addition

An addition the customer withdraws before its parts are ordered or its labor starts is credited in full, with the reason "addition withdrawn"; after that point it stays due.

| Parts ordered or labor started at the time of withdrawal | Effect |
|---|---|
| neither | the addition charge is credited in full |
| either one | the addition stays due |

## 5. Boundaries with the insurer and the deductible

Customer-pay additions are never billed to the insurer and never reduce the deductible.

superseded_clauses: repair of damage unrelated to the claim (or of operations the insurer denied), charged at the amount on the written customer-pay estimate line
The customer's customer-pay addition consent for that amount is signed.
